 Dubai students can soon use Nol cards for online, in-store shopping across GCC
 The card, now rebranded as the New Dubai Student Card, will have the same features as a standard Nol Card
 PUBLISHED: Wed 11 Nov 2026, 6:00 AM 
 By: 
 Nasreen Abdulla 
 Add as a preferred
 source on Google Share:
 Students will be able to use their Nol cards to make online payments and shop at outlets across the GCC from December 2026, the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has announced. The card, now rebranded as the New Dubai Student Card, will have the same features as a standard Nol Card, an RTA spokesperson confirmed to Khaleej Times .
 The upgrade means students can top up instantly through online channels, manage their profile, renew their card online, and allow parents to manage their account or card, the RTA said.

   The Nol Student Card has long offered a 50 per cent discount on public transport in Dubai, a key draw for school and university students across the emirate. Students can also access retail savings by registering for the Nol Plus loyalty programme through RTA's digital channels.
 Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels. 
 One card, three functions
 The New Dubai Student Card was launched by the RTA in collaboration with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA), TECOM Group's Dubai International Academic City and Dubai Knowledge Park, and the International Student Identity Card Association (ISIC).
 Ahmed Bahrozyan, CEO of RTA's Corporate Technology Services Sector, said the card brings together three core functions: student identification for engaging educational institutions, Nol public transport functionality, and internationally recognised student status through ISIC.
 "This card is designed to support students throughout their educational journey, offering benefits across four key areas," Bahrozyan said. These are:
 On campus: Student identification through participating educational institutions
 Around Dubai: RTA public transport with student fare discounts of up to 50 per cent
 Every day: Student benefits, discounts and offers across the UAE
 While travelling: More than 150,000 ISIC benefits across over 130 countries
 The initiative will be rolled out in phases. Educational institutions interested in participating can submit applications through www.dubaistudentcard.ae. 
 When was the Nol Student Card launched?
 The Nol Student Card was launched in 2009, soon after the launch of Dubai Metro . According to the RTA, 43,800 cards have been printed since 2024, and 49,500 cards are currently active.
 As per the figured, some metro stations are more popular than others among students. The top five metro stations for Nol Student Card users are:
 Burjuman Metro Station
 Stadium Metro Station
 Oud Metha Metro Station
 Dubai Internet City Metro Station
 City Centre Deira Metro Station
 How to apply for Nol Student Card
 Any school or university student in the UAE under the age of 23 can apply for the card on the RTA website or via the Nol pay app. Students have to submit their Emirates ID, a photograph and an official, stamped ‘Student Confirmation Letter’ from the school, college, or university. 
 A student Nol card costs Dh70 and is valid for five years.
 The RTA expanded the card's offering through the Nol ISIC card, which gives students privileges and global discounts in more than 130 countries. The ISIC integration was first announced in 2024, when the RTA partnered with the International Student Identity Card Association to roll out a card that doubles as internationally accepted student identification.
 At the time, the RTA said the package would offer students discounts of up to 70 per cent on local and international brands, alongside the existing 50 per cent public transport discount. 
 Global Benefits 
 Through the ISIC partnership, the card gives students internationally recognised proof of student status and access to discounts covering travel, accommodation, dining, entertainment, shopping and education.
 Matthew East, CEO of GTS ALIVE Group at ISIC, said: "Students today are connected to a world that extends far beyond their campus, and their student identity should reflect that. Through ISIC, the New Dubai Student Card gives students a globally recognised proof of student identity, connecting them with access to benefits, experiences and opportunities in Dubai and around the world."
 Dr Saeed Mubarak Kharbash, CEO of Policies, Research and Programmes at KHDA, said the card "puts the learner at the heart of the student experience, bringing together education, mobility, services and opportunities in a single student card".
 Marwan Abdulaziz Janahi, Senior Vice President of Dubai International Academic City and Dubai Knowledge Park, said the initiative "is designed to enhance the educational journey for learners, reinforcing Dubai's position as a global centre for higher education".
 A system-wide upgrade
 The student card's December upgrade comes as the RTA undertakes a broader modernisation of the Nol system. The authority has been transitioning to account-based ticketing technology, with plans to allow commuters to link Nol cards to digital accounts, use QR code ticketing, and pay fares through bank cards and digital wallets.
 The RTA has also announced a new generation of Nol-Jaywan cards, combining the Nol transport system with the UAE's national payment scheme, with a pilot beginning in November 2026 . Those cards will offer access to more than 120 promotional offers and exclusive discounts.
 For students, the December change means the Nol Student Card will no longer be limited to transport and campus canteens. It will function as a broader payment tool, both online and at physical outlets across the region.
